subject: chemistry
title: Electrolysis of molten ionic compounds
key_idea: When a molten binary ionic compound is electrolysed with inert electrodes, the metal forms at the negative electrode and the non-metal forms at the positive electrode. Positive metal ions are attracted to the cathode. Negative non-metal ions are attracted to the anode.

blocks.text: This section covers how to name the product at each electrode for a molten binary ionic compound.

items.meaning: A compound made of two elements, such as lead bromide, PbBr₂.
Melted, so the ions are free to move.
An electrode that does not react, so it only carries the current.

items: The compound must be molten. A solid cannot be electrolysed because its ions cannot move.
The **metal** forms at the cathode (negative electrode).
The **non-metal** forms at the anode (positive electrode).
Name the element, not the ion: write chlorine, not chloride. Halogens form molecules such as Cl₂ and Br₂.

diagram.alt: Choose a molten compound to see the product at each electrode.

options.label: Lead bromide
results: Pb²⁺ is positive and goes to the cathode. Br⁻ is negative and goes to the anode.

options.label: Zinc chloride
results: Zn²⁺ is positive and goes to the cathode. Cl⁻ is negative and goes to the anode.

options.label: Sodium chloride
results: Na⁺ is positive and goes to the cathode. Cl⁻ is negative and goes to the anode.

options.label: Copper chloride
results: Cu²⁺ is positive and goes to the cathode. Cl⁻ is negative and goes to the anode.

options.label: Potassium iodide
results: K⁺ is positive and goes to the cathode. I⁻ is negative and goes to the anode.

options.label: Magnesium bromide
results: Mg²⁺ is positive and goes to the cathode. Br⁻ is negative and goes to the anode.

items: Molten binary compound: metal at the negative electrode, non-metal at the positive electrode.
Write the element (chlorine, bromine), not the ion (chloride, bromide).

blocks.text: This section links the products to the movement of ions.

items: Metal ions are positively charged, so they are attracted to the negative electrode.
Non-metal ions are negatively charged, so they are attracted to the positive electrode.
A molten metal halide, such as potassium bromide, contains only a metal and a halogen. Hydrogen and oxygen cannot form from it.
Hydrogen can form instead of a metal only when the compound is in solution, because water supplies hydrogen ions.

blocks.text: In the laboratory and in industry

items: Molten lead bromide is electrolysed in a fume cupboard, because the bromine fumes are toxic.
Anhydrous zinc chloride is a safer alternative for practical work.
(Higher tier) In industry the products are kept apart, so that they do not react together and form the compound again.
Ions move to the electrode with the opposite charge.
Halogen fumes such as bromine are toxic, so the electrolysis is done in a fume cupboard.

checks.q: Name the product at each electrode when molten magnesium chloride is electrolysed.
checks.a: Negative electrode: magnesium. Positive electrode: chlorine.

checks.q: Why is the metal formed at the negative electrode?
checks.a: Metal ions are positively charged, so they are attracted to the negative electrode.

checks.q: Why is the electrolysis of molten lead bromide done in a fume cupboard?

exam_phrases: the ions cannot move / the ions are in fixed positions
so the products do not react (to reform sodium chloride)

mistakes.wrong: The product at the positive electrode is chloride.
mistakes.right: Chloride and Cl⁻ are not accepted. Write chlorine (Cl₂ or Cl is allowed). The same applies to bromine, not bromide.

mistakes.wrong: Copper is made at the positive electrode and chlorine at the negative electrode.
mistakes.right: If the two elements are reversed, only 1 of the 2 marks can be awarded. The metal forms at the negative electrode and the non-metal at the positive electrode.

mistakes.wrong: The teacher uses a fume cupboard because the fumes are dangerous.
mistakes.right: Dangerous, deadly and lethal are ignored. Write that the fumes are toxic or poisonous (harmful or corrosive are also allowed).

worked_example.question:
Molten copper chloride can be electrolysed.

State the product at each electrode when molten copper chloride is electrolysed.
answer_points: Positive electrode: chlorine (Cl₂ or Cl is allowed).
worked_example.tip: Chloride and Cl⁻ are not accepted. If the elements are the wrong way round, 1 mark is available.

exam_phrases: chlorine at the anode and zinc at the cathode
lead is produced at the cathode
bromine is produced at the anode
oxygen cannot be produced by the electrolysis of this molten salt
hydrogen cannot be produced by the electrolysis of this molten salt

mistakes.wrong: The electrolysis of molten potassium bromide gives hydrogen and oxygen.
mistakes.right: Neither hydrogen nor oxygen can be a product of molten potassium bromide. The products are potassium and bromine.

mistakes.wrong: Bromine is produced at the cathode when molten lead bromide is electrolysed.
mistakes.right: Lead is produced at the cathode. Bromine is produced at the anode.

worked_example.question:
A sample of molten potassium bromide is electrolysed.

What are the two products formed?
answer_points: Neither hydrogen nor oxygen is a product of this electrolysis.
worked_example.tip: This was a multiple-choice question. Only the pair potassium and bromine is correct.

exam_phrases: do not allow chloride / Cl / Cl⁻, allow Cl₂
allow Pb, do not allow Pb²⁺

mistakes.wrong: The product at the positive electrode is bromide.
mistakes.right: Bromide is not allowed. Write bromine. For potassium chloride the product is chlorine (Cl₂ is allowed, but chloride, Cl and Cl⁻ are not).

mistakes.wrong: The product at the negative electrode is Pb²⁺.
mistakes.right: Pb²⁺ is not allowed. The product is the element, lead (Pb).

mistakes.wrong: Solid aluminium oxide cannot be electrolysed because its electrons cannot move.
mistakes.right: Electrons cannot move is ignored. Say the ions cannot move.

A teacher demonstrates the electrolysis of molten lead bromide.

Predict the products made at each electrode.

Positive electrode ______
Negative electrode ______
worked_example.tip: Bromide is not allowed. If the two are reversed, 1 mark is available.
